First, let's factor the expression as a perfect square trinomial in $x^2.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}+18{x}^{2}+81 & ={({x}^{2})}^{2}+2\cdot 9\cdot \,({x}^{2})+(9)^{2} \\  & ={({x}^{2}+9)}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to factor the sum of squares in the parentheses. To do this, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using $\textrm{i}^2 = -1.$ Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+9 & ={x}^{2}-(-9) \\  & ={x}^{2}-(9{\text{i}}^{2}) \\  & ={x}^{2}-{(3\text{i})}^{2} \\  & =(x+3\text{i})(x-3\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this back into our main expression, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}+18{x}^{2}+81 & ={({x}^{2}+9)}^{2} \\  & =((x+3\text{i})(x-3\text{i}))^{2} \\  & =(x+3\text{i})^{2}(x-3\text{i})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
